findings.body: The first question round still creates Forge's status commit before calling Codex: worker.py:84–86 writes and commits the working state. The new question test explicitly expects HEAD's commit count to increase by one. This violates the supplied Done-when requirement that the round add no commit of its own. The source spec permits this pre-turn commit, but that exception is absent from the authoritative review contract. Defer the state commit or otherwise make question rounds satisfy the requested no-commit behavior.
findings.title: Not done: 2. A question round adds no commit of its own

findings.body: The answering-round test never verifies successful continuation. Its app-server stub rejects thread/resume as unsupported (tests/stubs/codex-app-server:134–135), so the answer always exercises a fresh conversation. Consequently, always starting fresh specifically when answering a question would pass this test. Add a question-and-answer case using the resumable fixture and assert that the answer uses the original conversation without starting another one.
findings.title: Not done: test_2_answer_continues_the_same_conversation

findings.body: The test covers a reported failed answer, but never interrupts an answering turn. The required interruption behavior therefore has no coverage: the question must remain recorded, and both work without --note and close must continue refusing. Add a command-level interruption case and verify those refusals afterward; a reported failed status does not exercise interruption and cleanup.
